subject: Anthropology
title: Fundamentalism
description: A fast breakdown of Fundamentalism for builders.

hook.text: Return to the pure origins. Reject compromise. Fight modernity. Fundamentalism appears in every major religion.

buildup.text: Fundamentalism is a reaction against modernity that demands strict return to what believers see as core scriptures.

discovery.text: It emerged in Protestant Christianity, but parallel movements exist in Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, and Buddhism.

twist.text: Fundamentalism is itself modern. It uses technology, media, and political organizing — the very tools of modernity.

climax.text: Fundamentalism isn't a return to the past. It's a modern reaction to modernity using modern tools to fight change.

punchline.text: Rejecting modernity is itself a modern act.

quiz.question: What is fundamentalism a reaction against?

details.summary: Fundamentalism is a modern reaction against perceived threats from secularism, modernity, and liberalism. Rather than a return to tradition, it selectively retrieves and reinterprets religious texts to create a militant defense of what adherents define as essential truths.
details.whyItMatters: Fundamentalism shapes global politics from American evangelicalism to Islamic movements. Understanding it as a modern phenomenon rather than ancient tradition is essential for analyzing contemporary religious conflicts.
takeaways: Fundamentalism is a modern reaction, not a return to tradition
It selectively retrieves religious texts for contemporary battles
It shapes global politics across multiple religious traditions

faq.question: Why do anthropologists say fundamentalism is modern rather than traditional?
faq.answer: Fundamentalists use modern media, organizational techniques, and political strategies. They select specific traditions to defend while ignoring others. Their literal approach to scripture is itself a modern interpretive choice. Traditional religions were far more flexible and contextual.

faq.question: Does fundamentalism appear in all religions?
faq.answer: Yes. Christian, Islamic, Jewish, Hindu, and Buddhist fundamentalisms all exist. Each responds to perceived threats from modernity and secularism by asserting selective religious authority. The pattern is cross-cultural, not limited to any one tradition.
